conventions.convention: Primitive exponents are positive, angular multi-indices start at zero, and contractions are finite complex linear combinations, including the empty sum.
All integral expressions are Lebesgue integrals. Bras are conjugated; f_ab = conjugate(phi_a) phi_b and G_ab,cd = C(f_ab,f_cd), with C conjugate-linear in its first density.
V_C is the positive-kernel integral without a built-in nuclear charge or minus sign; nuclear attraction combinations have separately specified signed real weights.
F_m(T) is defined for real T and nonnegative integer m, but the conventional Boys domain and evaluator domain are T ≥ 0. The real extension supports ordinary center derivatives at T = 0.
Hermite derivatives are with respect to the Gaussian center P; R^n_tuv = (-2η)^n times the indicated center derivative of F_n(η|P-C|²).
The energy and gradient functional uses real matrices and tensors, dimensions n,r ≥ 1, and the ordinary Euclidean gradient with respect to C. It asserts no physical or stationary-state postulate.

Boys recurrence endpoints are computed by exact rational affine arithmetic followed by one outward conversion. Zero arguments use directly rounded rational values, and overflowing candidate endpoints do not establish a range failure.

Screening visits ordered input-basis quartets without unrecorded symmetry compression. Diagonal bounds include every primitive contraction coefficient; entry bounds Q and weighted energy bounds w are accumulated and tested separately.

load_bearing.statement: For every nonnegative integer m and real T, F_m(T) has the stated convergent power series and derivative F'_m(T) = -F_(m+1)(T), with F_m(0) = 1/(2m+1). For T > 0, 2T F_(m+1)(T) = (2m+1)F_m(T) - exp(-T) and F_m(T) = γ(m+1/2,T)/(2T^(m+1/2)).

Every overlap, kinetic, point-nucleus attraction, and two-electron Coulomb integral defined in [[def-cartesian-gaussian-primitives-and-contractions]] exists absolutely for finite Cartesian Gaussian contractions.

The Hermite Coulomb auxiliaries satisfy R^n_(t+1,u,v) = (P₁-C₁)R^(n+1)_tuv + tR^(n+1)_(t-1,u,v), with corresponding coordinate formulas and negative-index terms zero. The stated finite Hermite sums equal the primitive nuclear-attraction and two-electron Coulomb integrals; the largest Boys order is bounded by the total participating polynomial degree.

The Coulomb form is Hermitian positive-semidefinite on the finite linear span of Gaussian pair densities, and |C(f,g)|² ≤ C(f,f)C(g,g). For any finite set S of omitted input-basis quartets in the real energy contraction, B_S = (1/2)Σ_S |W_ab W_cd| sqrt(G_ab,ab G_cd,cd) bounds the absolute omitted energy contribution.

For n,r ≥ 1, real C,D with Frobenius norms at most B,M, and entrywise tensor errors at most ε₂,ε₄, the energy error is at most MrnB²ε₂ + (1/2)M²r²n²B⁴ε₄, and the gradient Frobenius error is at most 2nrBMε₂ + 2n²r²B³M²ε₄.

Every call to the Boys evaluator terminates within its declared caps. On success, every returned I_m contains the exact range of F_m over the input interval and satisfies the required absolute and any reported relative accuracy. No success for every finite input or cap is asserted.
